subject: Discovery sync — evaluation goals & proposed POC scope (AurionX)
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery sync — evaluation goals & proposed POC scope (AurionX)

Hi Samir / Lena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you called out
- 30–40% of customer support routing misclassifications; manual triage overhead.
- Latency spikes when previewing suggestions inside your app (goal <= 250ms 95th).
- Cost sensitivity for high-volume inference (especially during peak hours).

Primary goals for the 6-week evaluation
1) Reduce routing misclassifications by >= 20% on the evaluation dataset.
2) Achieve median generation latency under 120ms and 95th under 250ms for 1–2k concurrent sessions.
3) Verify end-to-end integration with your SaaS UI and measure per-API token cost reduction via caching/batching.

Proposed POC scope (what Redwood will deliver)
- 6-week sandbox: hosted Dedicated instance sized for 2x expected concurrent load.
- Prompt/eval plan: we will run the 3 prompt families we discussed (intent classification, follow-up suggestion, and reranking) against your 5k labeled examples and the 1k unlabeled traffic sample.
- Metrics tracked: classification F1, rerank precision@3, latency (p50/p95), tokens/sec, and per-request cost.
- Failure-mode testing: adversarial prompt set and latency-degradation scenarios.

AurionX responsibilities (minimum for kickoff)
- Provide a 5k labeled CSV (format: id,text,label) and a 1k representative traffic anonymized sample.
- Whitelist our IPs and provision a read-only S3 bucket or presigned URL for data ingest.
- Confirm required compliance docs (SOC2 scope / data handling constraints).

Owners and timeline
- Redwood: Ava Chen (sales lead), Ben Carter (technical lead), Grace O'Connor (CS/success).
- AurionX: Samir Kapoor (product), Lena Ortiz (security/compliance).
- Proposed kickoff: Week of Apr 18 — 30 business days to baseline + 6 weeks for evaluation.

Attachments: attached a short POC plan (aurionx_poc_plan.pdf) and a draft mutual-action plan (redwood_mam_draft.docx).

Next steps
- Samir: confirm data availability and SOC2 gating items by Wed Apr 14.
- Redwood: provision sandbox and send access checklist once data window is confirmed.
- Tentative kickoff meeting on Apr 19 (30–45 min) to finalize owners and runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Ava — this is a very clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data & volume
- We can get you the 5k labeled examples by EOD Apr 15. The 1k traffic sample will require redaction; target for that is Apr 16.

2) Security/compliance
- Our security team needs to confirm whether Redwood can store the anonymized traffic in a US-region bucket (we can allow it, but SOC2 attachments + DPA routing are required).
- Can you send the SOC2 cover page and your DPA excerpt? That would help speed internal approval.

3) SLA/latency expectations
- The latency targets look right; one caveat — our UI sometimes spawns parallel requests for the same session. We'll share a short trace sample to help with batching recommendations.

4) Kickoff
- Apr 19 works for us at 10:00 AM PT. Samir (me) and Lena will attend; I may invite our infra lead if there are outstanding security questions.

We'll confirm the data delivery and accept the draft MAM after a quick pass. Looking forward to the kickoff.

—Samir
